narrative:
The model estimates a 63% chance that you will leave your current job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key aspects of your professional profile that, according to patterns seen across many similar employees, tend to signal higher turnover risk.

Most influential was your total years of experience. With 6–10 years overall, you sit in a range where people are more likely to explore new opportunities than those with very short careers. This factor pushed the prediction noticeably toward leaving. Closely behind it was the length of time you have spent in your current organization—only 1–5 years. Employees who have not yet built a long tenure here are statistically more mobile, and this also pulled the outcome toward departure.

The third strongest influence was that you have received other job offers while working here. Having external opportunities available strongly increases the likelihood the model assigns to leaving, as it reflects real-world alternatives that many who stay simply do not possess.

Taken together, these three elements—your solid but not extensive overall experience, relatively short time with the company, and access to outside offers—outweighed the many positive signals in your profile such as high recognition, strong emotional commitment, and satisfaction with your rewards.

The organization should consider discussing retention options with you, while you may wish to reflect on whether your current role still aligns with your longer-term goals. Addressing these specific mobility drivers could change the outlook for both sides.
